answer: To secure an economy of autonomous AI agents against Sybil attacks, networks can employ a cryptographic proof-of-work mechanism anchored to unique hardware enclaves. Like anchoring a sturdy jetty against turbulent tides, this forces malicious actors to mine through dense computational shale to mint identities. Before granting transactional privileges, the protocol forces each node to whisper a zero-knowledge proof verifying distinct physical silicon, ensuring that infinitely scalable software agents cannot artificially bloat the consensus without incurring prohibitive energy costs.
